title: Price chart
intro: The quote page has no chart of its own; the only chart is the full-screen TradingView page in a shared native WebView. Its first open is a strict chain: route push, loadPage in a post-frame callback, a fresh HTML fetch (unique &t= on every navigation), WebView/Chromium start, the 1.2-3.1 MB library, then history. The library prefetch that would take the network out of that chain exists but is off in prod. These changes add a Flutter inline chart (it needs a price-history API), warm the full-chart path while the user is on the quote page, and stop the hidden chart page and the quote page under the chart from doing work. The fixes on this branch (plugin 0.0.4 delegate claim, probe/recover, resume rewarm, strictly increasing t=, watchdogs) are kept as they are.

measured.metric: Inline chart on the quote page
measured.expected: visible <= 0.5 s after the page opens

measured.metric: Full chart, first open in a process

changes.title: Add a price-history source for the quote page
changes.summary: Nothing in mo_get_quote fetches a price time series, so an inline chart has no data. Agree an endpoint with the backend (check the unused PriceMovementLineChart message first) and add one repository method.
changes.risk_reason: New endpoint and a new repository method; nothing existing calls it until G3 ships behind its flag.
changes.be_request: Provide price history for one scrip and range: 1D (1-5 min points, intraday so far), 1W, 1M, 1Y, 5Y; at most about 300 points per range; protobuf like other quote APIs; Cache-Control max-age about 60 s for 1D and about 1 h for longer ranges. First answer: is PriceMovementLineChartResponse (trader_proto_gen proto/Quote/QuoteModels.proto:244-265, fields updateTime, price, open/high/low...) served by any live endpoint today? If yes, share the URL, auth and which fields are filled; if not, name the existing history API the app may call with the same token (the TradingView datafeed is not callable from Dart today).

files.change: Add priceHistory URL constant (name per BE answer).
Add fetchPriceHistory to the interface.
Implement fetchPriceHistory with the same apiCall pattern, cache-first.
Small model (List of time/price points, range) mapped from the proto.

changes.current: The repository fetches overview, fundamentals, dashboard and getQuote (e.g. fetchQuoteOverviewData, mo_get_quote_repository_impl.dart:107-123) but no time series. PriceMovementLineChart is defined in QuoteModels.proto:244-265 and has no Dart caller outside generated files.
steps: Send the BE request above; until answered, build G2/G3 against a mock repository (rules: @Injectable(as: ..., env: [Environment.dev]), 300-800 ms delay).
Add the URL constant, interface method and implementation using apiCall(..., isForcedCacheEnable: true) so a reopen shows the last points at once.
Map the proto to PriceHistory with only (time, price) to keep the painter input small.
Live point: G3 appends from the page's tick at most once per second; no new socket subscription.
safety: Additive: new constant, new interface method, new model; no existing call changes.
Not called by any screen until G3's flag is on.
regression_checks: Unit test: PriceHistory.fromProto with empty, single-point and 300-point responses.
Mock and real implementations both registered correctly (dev vs default env).
changes.after_improvement: Gives the inline chart its data in one small cached call; target payload a few KB per range.

Barrel export.

changes.title: Add an inline line chart below the price card
changes.summary: Show a lightweight Flutter line chart (ranges 1D/1W/1M/1Y/5Y) under the stock info card, with its own cubit so it does not wait for the page load. Behind a flag.
changes.risk_reason: Adds height to the header: the hard-coded scroll thresholds and sticky positions (mo_get_quote_screen.dart:105-127, sticky_chips_section.dart:64) assume today's header height, so the sticky tabs would snap at the wrong place unless the header is measured (section B). Flag off keeps today's layout.
changes.product_decision: Approve an inline price chart under the price card: ranges (proposed 1D/1W/1M/1Y/5Y, default 1D), height (proposed 160 dp), line colour (up/down for the selected range), what a tap or long-press does (proposed: long-press scrubs, tap opens the full chart), which asset types get it (proposed cash and index first; F&O, currency, commodity later), and the closed-market/empty state. Ship behind Remote Config quote_inline_chart_enabled (default false).
changes.be_request: Remote Config: add boolean quote_inline_chart_enabled (default false). Data per G1.

files.change: Insert the inline chart after _buildStockInfo when the flag is on.
MoCustomLineChart (trader_widgets) + range chips, RepaintBoundary, design tokens.
Own cubit/state (loading, loaded, empty, error) keyed by scrip and range; caches each range for the page's lifetime.
Add inlineChartEnabled hook.

Offline and empty-history states.

changes.title: Warm the chart path when a quote page opens
changes.summary: The WebView is pre-warmed once at app start and the library prefetch runs on app start, login and resume only. When a quote page opens, make sure the WebView still exists and the library warm-up has run, without loading any page.
changes.risk_reason: Adds one idempotent platform call (prewarm) and one warm-up trigger at quote open, in the shared chart package. It loads no page, so it cannot race ChartController; skipped while any chart is mounted.

files.change: Add static void Function()? onQuotePageShown hook (mo_get_quote cannot import trader_native_charts: that package imports mo_get_quote).
Call MoGetQuoteHooks.onQuotePageShown?.call() in the existing post-frame callback.
Add ensureWarm(reason): skip if a chart is mounted, at most once a minute, call prewarmCall() (reuses or recreates the WebView and claims the delegate).
In install(), set the hook to ensureWarm + ChartLibraryWarmer.warm(trigger: 'quoteOpen', requireStoredUrl: true).

changes.current: main_common.dart:562-571 calls ChartPrewarmService.warmup() (WebView only, deliberately no page, chart_prewarm_service.dart:17-24) and ChartLibraryWarmer.warm(trigger: 'appStart'); main_common.dart:1179 retries on resume. If the OS reclaimed the WebView or its renderer since start, the first chart tap pays WebView creation (about 4 s cold). Opening a quote page is the strongest signal that a chart tap may follow, and nothing uses it.
steps: Add ChartPrewarmService.ensureWarm(reason) with the guards in after_code.
Add the hook in mo_get_quote and call it once per quote page from the post-frame callback in initState.
Wire the hook in ChartLibraryPrefetch.install(); ChartLibraryWarmer.warm is already one-at-a-time, bounded to 3 attempts and a no-op once done.
Log 'ensureWarm quoteOpen created=...' in Hive to see how often the WebView had to be recreated.
safety: No page load: keeps the reason ChartPrewarmService documents for never loading a page (PageReady to nobody, 0x0 viewport).
Skipped whenever a full or mini chart is registered, the same rule rewarm uses.
Throttled to once a minute and never throws; a failure just leaves today's first-open cost.
Library warm-up keeps its own Remote Config gate (G5) and budget.
regression_checks: Open 10 quote pages quickly: at most one prewarm call per minute in the Hive log.
Quote -> chart -> quote (market-depth header from the chart) -> chart: no stuck loader.
Kill the WebView renderer (adb) on a quote page, then tap chart: opens without the 4 s cold create.
changes.after_improvement: WebView creation (about 4 s cold) moves off the first chart tap whenever the user was on a quote page first; with G5 on, the library download is also off the tap.

changes.title: Turn on chart_lib_prefetch_enabled in prod
changes.summary: The chart library prefetch is fully built and wired to Remote Config, but the flag is off, so a new install or a cleared cache downloads 1.2-3.1 MB on the first chart tap. Turn it on with a staged rollout (L4).
changes.risk_reason: Config only; the warmer is bounded (3 attempts, 3 min timeout, yields to a loading chart) and the flag is the rollback.
changes.be_request: Set Remote Config chart_lib_prefetch_enabled = true in prod with a staged rollout (10 % -> 50 % -> 100 % over a week). Before that, confirm chart-lib-manifest.json is published next to the prod chart page; a missing manifest only reports 'manifest missing' and does nothing. Watch the Firebase Performance trace chart_lib_warm for ok rate and bytes.

files.change: No code change: the flag is already read here.

changes.current: ChartLibraryPrefetch.isEnabled reads chart_lib_prefetch_enabled and any failure reads as off (chart_library_prefetch.dart:36-46); ChartLibraryWarmer.isEnabled defaults to off (chart_library_warmer.dart:60). Triggers exist for appStart, login and resume.
steps: Publish/verify the manifest on the prod chart host.
Enable for 10 %, compare first-open chart time (Hive 'state ... +Xms' lines) between groups.
Ramp to 100 % if no rise in chart errors or data complaints.
safety: Flag is the rollback; no release needed.
Warm-up runs in a separate throwaway WebView inside the plugin and never touches the chart's WebView.
ChartController._beginPageLoad stops a running warm-up so it never competes with a chart load.
regression_checks: New install: login, then first chart open; library served from cache (no 1.2-3.1 MB on the tap).
Mobile data usage at login stays within the expected 1.2-3.1 MB once per install/cache clear.
changes.after_improvement: Removes the library download from the first chart open for new installs and cleared caches; parsing still happens on first run.

changes.title: Split the cold-open time; make the first URL cacheable
changes.summary: Every navigation adds a unique &t=, so the chart HTML is never served from the WebView cache. The uniqueness is load-bearing for retries and the iOS same-URL skip, so keep it for every navigation except the first one of a process, and only after measuring that the HTML fetch matters.
changes.risk_reason: Navigation identity is what the iOS plugin's same-URL skip and retryPageLoad's cancel-by-new-URL depend on (chart_controller.dart:565-569, 651-657). Changing it in the shared controller could bring back a silent no-op load. Behind a flag, first navigation only.
changes.be_request: Chart web team: send Cache-Control (for example max-age=300, must-revalidate with ETag) on the chart HTML page; WebView cacheMode is LOAD_DEFAULT, so without it a stable URL gains nothing. Remote Config: add boolean chart_versioned_first_url (default false).

files.change: First navigation of the process (loadAttempt == 1, no earlier URL) uses &v=<release>; all others keep the strictly increasing &t=.

changes.current: getChartCompleteUrl (chart_controller.dart:571-589) always appends &t=<seconds>, forced strictly increasing because the iOS plugin skips webView.load when the URL equals the current one (565-569), and retryPageLoad relies on a new URL to cancel a hung navigation (651-657). Watchdogs: PageReady 20 s and Chart 25 s (full_view_chart.dart:114-118), Chart-reply grace 8 s (291, only subscribes ticks), native ack 3 s (chart_controller.dart:91). None of them adds time to a healthy load; they act only on a stall, so the 8-13 s first chart is cold WebView + HTML + library + history, plus a recovery in runs that stalled (verify).
steps: Measure first: from a benchmark run's Hive log, take 'page load #1', 'loadRequested', 'PageReady +Xms', 'Chart loaded +Xms' and any 'load stalled' lines to split the 8-13 s. If a stall/recovery appears, fix that first; it is not a watchdog timing problem.
Only if the HTML fetch is > about 300 ms and BE has added Cache-Control: add the versioned first URL behind chart_versioned_first_url.
Keep &t= for retries, reloads, recover() and every later navigation.
safety: Flag default false: URL generation is exactly today's.
Only the first navigation of a process changes; the strictly increasing t= rule for every later navigation is kept.
No change to watchdog durations or recovery logic from commit 083141c.
regression_checks: iOS and Android: first open, then retry from the stall UI, then reload on resume; each navigation actually loads.
Self-heal tests in trader_native_charts (chart_controller_self_heal_test.dart) pass; add one for the first-URL branch.
Theme switch before the first open (URL theme parameter still applied).
changes.after_improvement: If confirmed, the first open in a process reads the HTML from the WebView cache, saving one network round trip plus the HTML download; the measured phase split tells how much of the 8-13 s each step costs.

changes.title: Preload the chart page from the quote page
changes.summary: Optional second step after G4: while the user is on a quote page, navigate the warmed WebView to the chart page with a real viewport, and let the chart screen adopt a page that is already loaded. Behind a flag.
changes.risk_reason: Changes when the shared chart page loads and adds a path where PageReady arrives before any screen is registered. Today that path would leave the chart blank (loadingCharts ignores pageLoaded), so the screen side must change in the same release.
changes.be_request: Remote Config: add boolean chart_page_preload_enabled (default false).

files.change: loadingCharts also loads the chart when the state is pageLoaded (page preloaded before this screen existed).

Add preloadPage(viewport): only when flag on, no screen registered and state initial; navigates through IosWebViewPlugin.prewarm(url:, width:, height:) and arms the ack timer. loadPage skips a second navigation if a preload is in flight for < 20 s.
Hook (G4) also calls preloadPage after ensureWarm, when the flag is on.

changes.current: ChartPrewarmService loads no page on purpose (chart_prewarm_service.dart:17-24): a PageReady with no listener, a 0x0 detached viewport, and loadPage trusting its own state. PageReady with no callback sets state pageLoaded only (chart_controller.dart:394-408); the screen then calls loadPage, which is skipped (632-636), and loadingCharts acts only on chartLoaded/chartError (full_view_chart.dart:269-278), so no loadChart would be sent. The plugin's prewarm already accepts url, width and height and lays the WebView out before loading (WebViewMoFlutterViewFactory.kt:595-640).
steps: Change loadingCharts so pageLoaded also triggers loadChart (guarded by the flag).
Add ChartController.preloadPage(viewport) using IosWebViewPlugin.prewarm(url, javascriptChannels: ['ChartAppDelegate'], width, height) so the page gets a real viewport.
In loadPage, if a preload is still pageLoading and started < 20 s ago, skip the new navigation and let the screen's watchdog bound it; otherwise behave as today.
Call preloadPage from the G4 hook after ensureWarm, only on Wi-Fi or when the user opened a chart in the last N sessions (Product may tune).
Use probePage() before adopting a preloaded page after a long time on the quote page; recover() already adopts a live page.
safety: Flag chart_page_preload_enabled defaults to false; with it off loadingCharts and loadPage behave exactly as today.
Never preloads while any chart is registered or once a page is loading/loaded.
Ships only after G4 and the G6 measurement show the page load is still the largest cold cost.
Self-heal (probe/recover) stays the path for a page that went bad between preload and open.
regression_checks: Flag on: quote page -> wait 3 s -> chart: candles drawn without a second navigation (log shows one 'page load #').
Flag on: tap chart within 300 ms of opening the quote page (preload in flight).
Flag on: preload, background 2 h with push, resume, open chart (probe/recover path).
Mini chart (F&O index view) and full chart both after a preload.
Theme change between preload and open.
changes.after_improvement: Takes page load and library parse off the tap when the user spends a few seconds on the quote page first; target first open <= 2 s (verify on the benchmark device).

changes.title: Pause the detached chart page after leaving
changes.summary: After the chart is closed the WebView is only detached, so the page keeps its rendering work. When no chart is registered for 30 s, call WebView.onPause() on that one WebView; the plugin already resumes it in getOrCreateWebView.
changes.risk_reason: Native plugin and shared controller. The plugin comment says not pausing keeps touch responsive; resume must happen before the WebView is re-attached. pauseTimers() must not be used: it is process-global and would stop every WebView in the app.
changes.be_request: Remote Config: add boolean chart_pause_on_leave_enabled (default false).

files.change: Add pausePage(): only when detached and not already paused; sets isWebViewPaused and calls webView.onPause().
Add a 'pausePage' method next to 'destroyWebView'.
Add IosWebViewPlugin.pausePage() (no-op on iOS and on older native sides via MissingPluginException).
clearCallback starts a 30 s timer when no screen is registered; setCallback cancels it.

changes.current: detachWebView deliberately does not pause (WebViewMoFlutterViewFactory.kt:887-891). resumeWebView (909-915) calls onResume/resumeTimers only when isWebViewPaused is true, which today happens only after destroyWebView. So after the chart closes, the page and its JS keep running for the session, and the quote page underneath shares the device's CPU with it.
steps: Measure first: CPU of the WebView renderer process for 2 minutes after closing the chart (Perfetto). A detached Chromium view may already throttle rAF; if the cost is near zero, drop this change.
Add pausePage() in the plugin (Android) using onPause() only; confirm in code that the platform view's attach path calls getOrCreateWebView/resumeWebView before showing.
Add the Dart method and the 30 s timer in ChartController, behind the flag.
Bump the plugin ref and pubspec.lock in the three pubspecs that name it, as commit 4a73f4e did.
safety: Flag default false; with it off no pause call is ever made.
onPause() only, never pauseTimers(), so KYC, payment and other WebViews are unaffected.
30 s grace keeps quick chart -> quote -> chart reopen on the unpaused page (warm reopen unchanged).
The detach-only dispose and the delegate-claim fix are not changed; destroy logic untouched.
regression_checks: Close chart, wait 60 s, reopen: chart responsive on first touch, candles update.
Close chart, open another WebView screen (KYC, research PDF): it loads and runs normally.
Pause, background 2 h with push, resume, open chart (self-heal path).
Flag off: no behaviour change.
changes.after_improvement: The chart page stops rendering work after the user leaves the chart (CPU to about 0, to be confirmed); memory is handled by F5.

changes.title: Restore quote streams when the chart closes
changes.summary: Opening the chart replaces the broadcaster's whole subscription set, and the quote page under it keeps rebuilding for the chart's ticks. Pause the quote page when the chart is pushed and re-subscribe its symbols when the chart's route completes.
changes.risk_reason: Changes when the quote page re-subscribes; a missed restore would leave a frozen price. Uses the F2 flag; with it off the code path is today's.

files.change: Call onPageHidden() before pushNamed and onPageVisible() when the awaited push completes (the chart was popped or removed).

changes.current: subscribeQuote unsubscribes every symbol not in the new set (mosl_broadcaster broadcast_controller.dart:248-258). FullViewChart subscribes the chart's symbols from onChartLoaded (full_view_chart.dart:883-907) and only cancels its own listener in dispose, so after Back the quote page's symbols are no longer subscribed unless one of its widgets happens to re-subscribe from build. navigateToCharts already awaits Navigator.pushNamed (mo_get_quote_cubit.dart:1795-1799), which completes when the chart route is popped.
steps: Before pushNamed: onPageHidden() (F2) stops depth and marks the page hidden, so ticks for the chart's symbol do not rebuild the hidden page's heavy sections.
After the await (in finally): if the cubit is not closed, onPageVisible() re-subscribes the page's symbol set and depth.
If F2's RouteAware ships, didPopNext does the same; keep only one of the two paths.
Verify on device: count 'Subscribe Quote' log lines after Back from the chart, and check the quote price ticks.
safety: Uses the F2 flag (default false); with it off the method is unchanged.
Re-subscribing a symbol that is still subscribed is a no-op request (subscription.addAll returns Request.empty).
finally also runs when MyNavigatorObserver removes a superseded chart route.
regression_checks: Quote -> chart -> Back: price, change and depth on the quote page tick again within one tick interval (live market).
Quote -> chart -> switch symbol tab in chart -> Back.
Chart rotated to landscape, then Back.
Quote -> chart -> depth header -> quote (replace path).
changes.after_improvement: No frozen quote price after returning from the chart, and the quote page does no tick work while the chart is on top.
